reasons: Deviation classification is correct: the original Section 15 requires the other party's prior written approval for any assignment with only an affiliate exception — it lacks the successor/M&A carve-out and the 'not unreasonably withheld' standard, so it fails the fallback on both material terms and edges toward walk-away (consent gate on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out).

Redline reaches the preferred position with edits tied to the rule: reasonableness standard on consent, affiliate/successor carve-out for Client on written notice, no Vendor assignment to a Client competitor, and express confirmation that a Client change of control is not an assignment and triggers no Vendor termination or re-pricing right — matching the redline guidance.
Narrowing the affiliate exception to 'assignment by Client' is within the rule's preferred position (Vendor may not assign without Customer consent) and benefits our party, so it is not over-reach.

The failed minimal-edit heuristic (0.690 changed-character ratio) is explained by the fact that the clause is a single short sentence and the rule requires adding several substantive carve-outs; the original operative language is preserved rather than replaced.
Comment is accurate, concise, first-person plural, prefixed correctly, explains the change, cites the playbook position and offers the notice-based mutual successor fallback.
